title: Granular entitlement matrix, quota rollover, and soft-overage safeguards
creator: Aisha Cooper
summary: Define and implement a granular entitlement matrix for plans (per-route, per-token-type, per-model), add a bounded monthly rollover for unused credits, and introduce a soft-overage grace mechanism that prevents immediate billing spikes while preserving observability for ops and finance.
background: Current plan entitlements are coarse-grained (monthly token buckets per account). Customers building hybrid workloads (embeddings + streaming generation + high-throughput reranking) request more predictable behavior: ability to set route-level quotas, let low-cost embeddings be counted differently than high-cost completion tokens, support limited rollover of unused credits, and avoid surprise invoices when transient bursts occur.
goals: 1) Surface a plan entitlement matrix that owners can configure per-product tier. 2) Implement 1-month rollover up to a configurable cap. 3) Introduce a soft-overage mode (grace buffer + billing reporting) that: a) permits short bursts without invoice charges, b) emits events to billing/ops, and c) provides clear UI/API signals to customers. 4) Ensure proration logic for mid-cycle plan changes is accurate and reconciled in billing exports.
non_goals: 1) International tax handling and multi-currency invoicing. 2) Deep discounts and complex reseller flows. 3) Long-term archival of detailed per-token usage beyond 90 days (separate observability project).
requirements:
- Plans can define entitlements at three axes: route (API path), token_type (embedding, completion, chat), and model_class (lite, standard, premium).
- Entitlement rows may include: monthly_quota, rollover_cap, soft_overage_buffer, per_unit_price_override, and priority_routing_flag.
- Rollover: unused monthly_quota is converted to rollover_credits up to rollover_cap and consumed before new monthly_quota.
- Soft-overage: when an account exceeds quota+soft_overage_buffer, allow service for up to N minutes (configurable per plan) and mark all tokens as 'soft_overage' in usage stream. Billing charges should be delayed but recorded as pending; if overage persists beyond grace window, convert pending charges to invoiceable charges.
- Expose entitlement matrix in Console (editable JSON grid) and via Admin API.
- Public-facing API and response headers should include quota_remaining and soft_overage_state for the request's scope.
- Billing export format (CSV/Parquet) must include columns: plan_id, account_id, route, token_type, model_class, month, quota_allocated, rollover_used, soft_overage_seconds, invoiceable_overage_units, proration_adjustment.
- Proration for mid-cycle upgrades/downgrades: calculate remaining entitlement and apply credit/debit on next invoice, with audit-friendly line items and a cancellation-downgrade path that preserves rollover rules.
out_of_scope:
- Per-customer bespoke pricing negotiations and manual adjustments (handled by Sales Ops).
- Building an accrual accounting system; billing exports suffice for finance reconciliation.
- ML model to predict overage risk (future project).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Admin Console shows the configurable entitlement matrix for at least three plans (Free, Growth, Enterprise) and allows editing of monthly_quota, rollover_cap, and soft_overage_buffer with immediate validation and preview of effective monthly limits.
AC-2: API responses to generation/embedding calls include X-Quota-Remaining and X-Soft-Overage-State headers with correct scoped values when requests are made at plan, route, and token_type levels.

AC-3: Rollover behavior: when a test account has unused quota in month M, a maximum of rollover_cap credits are moved to month M+1 and appear in Console and billing exports; automated unit tests and system tests validate at 0%, 50%, and 100% utilization scenarios.

AC-4: Soft-overage grace: simulate a sustained burst that exceeds quota by 30% for 10 minutes and verify that: a) requests succeed during grace window, b) usage events are flagged as soft_overage, c) pending charges appear in the billing pending queue but are not invoiced until grace window expires, and d) an email and console banner are emitted to the account admin when grace is active.

AC-5: Billing export contains required columns (as in requirements) and values reconcile to ledger for a sample month with mixed normal, rollover, and overage usage. Finance runs a reconciliation job on exported CSV and the delta is within 0.1% after rounding rules.

AC-6: Proration: mid-cycle upgrade from Growth->Enterprise shows correct credit for remaining Growth quota and charges Enterprise price prorated; line items are present in next invoice with clear description and testable math.
AC-7: Backwards compatibility: existing API keys without plan-scoped entitlements default to the legacy monthly token bucket behavior (no change) unless owner enables entitlement matrix via Console.
milestones: 1) Design review + entitlement schema finalized (2026-03-22). 2) Billing export schema and CSV contract agreed with Finance (2026-03-29). 3) Backend implementation of quota engine and soft-overage flags (ENG) (2026-04-12). 4) Console UI and Admin API changes (2026-04-15). 5) E2E QA, reconciliation tests, and docs (2026-04-22). 6) Release to staging and monitor 2 weeks before GA (2026-04-25).
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Soft-overage allows runaway costs for Redwood. Mitigation: require opt-in per account for soft-overage, default to opt-out for new accounts; set maximum soft_overage_buffer and grace_time per plan.
- Risk: Complex entitlement matrix increases operational surface. Mitigation: limit initial rollout to three plan templates and telemetry to measure misconfigurations; provide automated validation in Console.
- Risk: Finance reconciliation mismatches. Mitigation: iterative contract with Finance, sample end-to-end test data sets, and reconciliation alerts if monthly delta > 0.5%.
open_questions: Q1: Should soft-overage pending charges be visible to customers in real-time via Console, or only after grace window expires?
Q2: What is the default rollover_cap percentage for Growth and Enterprise tiers (suggest 20% Growth, 50% Enterprise)?
Q3: For hybrid requests (single API call that triggers embedding + completion), how should entitlements be split and billed (two line items or aggregated with weighted unit)?
Q4: Should grace windows be interruptible by Finance in exceptional cases (manual stop)?
implementation_notes:
- Backend: extend existing quota service with new dimension keys (route, token_type, model_class). Add soft-overage state machine and pending-charge queue.
- Billing: add new export columns and a small job to convert pending charges into invoiceable items once grace windows expire.
- Console: editable grid with preview and guardrails; show effective monthly limit calculations and rollover forecast.
- Observability: new metrics (soft_overage_events_total, rollover_applied_total, rollover_credits_active) and alerts for abnormal usage patterns.
- Docs: update public pricing docs and API reference with header semantics and examples.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for entitlement evaluation logic across dimensions.
- Integration tests simulating month boundaries and rollover flows.
- Chaos test: intermittent spikes during grace window to verify pending-charge behavior.
- Finance reconciliation test using seeded dataset and verification script.
- UX review and accessibility audit for Console changes.
